title: Setting a Travel Protection Plans Deductible against an Air Ticket Fare Brands Credit Release
content:
Where cover under the Travel Protection Plans was bought against an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking, the plan's per-claim deductible may be taken off the gross release. Two readings of the cover decide it: whether it has settled a claim over the last 12 months, and whether its per-claim deductible stands above zero.

## 1. What is taken off

| Where | What is taken off |
| --- | --- |
| protection cover bought against this booking is on file, has settled a claim in the last 12 months and carries a per-claim deductible above 0.00 USD | that deductible |
| such cover is on file, has settled no claim in that period and carries a per-claim deductible above 0.00 USD | 0.5 of that deductible, being 50 percent of it |
| in every other case | nothing, the deduction standing at 0.00 USD |

## 2. The two readings

The cover in question is a policy under the Travel Protection Plans standing on file against this air booking; its per-claim deductible is a term of the plan held. A claim settled inside the window is one recorded against that policy as paid over the 12 months back from today.

A plan whose per-claim deductible stands at 0.00 USD falls to the third row whatever its claims history, because both of the first two rows turn on a deductible above zero.

## 3. Worked figures, on hypothetical inputs

A plan on file against the booking carrying a per-claim deductible of a hypothetical 100.00 USD, with one claim paid 5 months ago: the whole 100.00 USD is taken off.

The same plan with no claim paid inside the window: 50.00 USD is taken off.

The same plan carrying a per-claim deductible of 0.00 USD, or no such plan on file at all: nothing is taken off.
